question: What exactly counts as knowability in relation to a manifest object?
premises: When consciousness converges on a manifest object, that convergence is called knowability.
Knowability is thus defined from the side of consciousness, not from the side of the object.
If knowability were a property of objects, it would belong to them independently of this convergence.
inference: Knowability is the conscious convergence on a manifest object, not a property of objects themselves.
plain_english: When consciousness comes together with a manifest object, that very event is what we call knowability. So we say knowability is not a property belonging to objects.
